new_entities.name: IV EDTA chelation
new_entities.description: Intravenous disodium EDTA or edetate-based chelation regimens promoted to reduce cardiovascular risk.

new_entities.name: Cardiovascular outcomes
new_entities.description: Clinical cardiovascular endpoints such as myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization, hospitalization, or cardiovascular death.

edges.effect_quant: In the original TACT randomized trial of 1,708 post-MI patients, EDTA chelation modestly lowered the composite cardiovascular endpoint versus placebo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.69-0.99), but the 2024 TACT2 replication in 1,000 patients with diabetes and prior MI did not reproduce a reduction in cardiovascular events. Cochrane-level reviews therefore rate the overall evidence as low-certainty and insufficient for routine use.
edges.population: older adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, especially prior myocardial infarction cohorts receiving repeated IV EDTA infusions
edges.mechanism: Chelation advocates propose removal of toxic metals or vascular calcium-related effects, but any biologic plausibility remains secondary to the inconsistent clinical-outcomes record.
edges.summary: This is a contested cardiovascular-intervention edge. One large randomized trial suggested a modest composite benefit, but replication has been poor and modern evidence does not support routine IV EDTA chelation as an established cardiovascular therapy.
edges.caveats: Do not present chelation as standard secondary prevention for cardiovascular disease. The apparent positive signal is heavily dependent on one older trial and is offset by lower-certainty evidence and failed replication.

evidence.citation: Diaz-Arocutipa C et al 2022 J Am Heart Assoc
